status: fixture-qualified and live-proven on a workstation against herdr 0.9.1; no controller loop calls the reconciler yet, so nothing runs on Anton
evidence_class: mocked cases run the catalog, the ownership store and the reconciler against a recording stand in for the herdr client; the live proof ran the pinned herdr 0.9.1 client against two worker sshds with supervised herdr servers on the operator workstation
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.herdr.catalog.Catalog(run) changes the client's saved machines only through herdr machine commands: machines() parses herdr machine list --json into Machine(profile_id, label, target, session, enabled) and refuses an unreadable listing (catalog_unreadable) instead of reading it as empty; add(label, target, session) runs herdr machine add --label L --remote-session S TARGET and returns the opaque profile id herdr prints (catalog_ambiguous when it names none, machine_refused when herdr refuses, catalog_unreachable when herdr does not answer); rename(id, label) runs herdr machine rename ID --label L; remove(id) runs herdr machine remove ID. herdr's own catalog file is never read or written

scripts.swarm_v2.herdr.reconcile.Store(path) is the controller ownership record beside the client terminal material (registrations.json, mode 0600, written atomically with fsync, guarded by an exclusive lock file): execution id, generation, label, target, session, profile id, and for an add whose outcome is unknown the profile ids listed before it. Only profiles it names are ever renamed or removed

scripts.swarm_v2.herdr.reconcile.Registrations.register(endpoint) saves one endpoint under its endpoint name with the explicit default remote session, refusing a label or target already held by a machine it does not own (label_collision, target_collision) and a generation older than the recorded one (stale_generation); it adopts an interrupted add only from a profile not listed before that add; withdraw(endpoint) removes the recorded profile; reconcile(desired, qualifier) registers the newest generation of every desired endpoint, removes a registration whose server qualifies incompatible, removes a registration added in this pass whose server cannot be reached (unreachable) and keeps a previously verified one, reporting it in Report.unverified, replaces a managed profile whose target or session moved, renames a drifted managed label back, restores a missing managed registration and removes managed registrations whose attempt is no longer desired, returning Report(registered, refused, retired, drift)

scripts.swarm_v2.herdr.attach.Terminal.attach(scope, host_public) now saves through Registrations.register and withdraws the registration when the qualifier verdict is incompatible, the incarnation was replaced or, for a registration this attach created, the server cannot be reached; Terminal.sync(attachable, enabled=...) writes the SSH client material and checks the connection for each attachable (scope, host key), then reconciles the client to exactly those endpoints; with enabled false it returns an empty report and runs no herdr command

scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.terminal.HostKeys.attachable(swarm, live) returns the launch recorded host key of every live execution; operator_sync(terminal, keys, principal, swarm, live, enabled=...) builds each scope with operator_scope, so only the operator role can synchronize the Anton herdr client
Registrations refuses an endpoint whose scope actor is neither a launch grant nor the operator role (unauthorized) before any herdr change

supported_versions.herdr: 0.9.1 linux x86_64, the SV2-HDR-01 pinned build; machine rename takes the profile id before --label, verified live (the reverse order exits 2)

authority: Actor and scope come from the SV2-HDR-02 terminal scope: a verified launch grant registration or an operator role principal. Registration labels and targets are derived from that scope's execution id; a label never grants ownership, only the controller ownership record does.
authoritative_objects: The herdr client's saved machine catalog is authoritative for what the operator sees and is changed only through herdr machine commands. The ownership record is authoritative for which saved machines the controller may rename or remove. Removing a machine leaves its remote herdr server and sessions running.

remaining_limitations: operator_sync is the synchronization entry point, but nothing calls it on a schedule yet: running it on controller start and on every attempt change, with the live execution set from the observed runtime and the drift gauge exported, belongs to task t376 (the master split it from this package), which builds on this branch.
Machines saved by the SV2-HDR-02 attach path before this change carry no ownership record and are refused as collisions until the operator removes them; no SV2-HDR-02 client was deployed.

After an add whose reply never arrived, a machine with the identical label, target and session that someone else saves before the retry would be adopted when the controller's own add was in fact lost; two such machines are refused as ambiguous. The label is controller generated, so the window is narrow.

The verdict incarnation is asserted by the caller from the terminal scope (one supervised herdr server per execution attempt, SV2-HDR-01); herdr does not report it, so case A check verdicts_keyed_by_endpoint_incarnation shows each verdict is keyed by its endpoint's incarnation, not that the server confirmed it.
Drift kind moved extends the spec's list: a managed profile whose target or session no longer matches its endpoint (a namespace change) is removed and added again, since herdr cannot edit a target.
The live proof ran on the operator workstation over localhost SSH with an injected resolver, not on Anton.
rollout_safety: Only the new registration path is affected; with no caller the local runtime and the SV2-HDR-02 terminal endpoint behave as before apart from the attach changes listed under compatibility.
